newsitem.title: USA: Gore, Kemp exchange opening shots in TV debate.
newsitem.headline: Gore, Kemp exchange opening shots in TV debate.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore and Republican Jack Kemp opened their campagin debate on Wednesday with amiable pledges to stay positive followed by immediate mutual attacks on policy issues.

Kemp, Bob Dole's vice presidential running mate, quickly took swipes at Democratic President Bill Clinton's leadership, saying, "Our foreign policy is ambivalent, confusing, it is sending wrong signals to the wrong people, and we've learned over the years that weakness is provocative."

Kemp also denigrated Clinton's economic policies as ones of over-taxation and weak growth, but Gore shot right back on that score by ridiculing the Dole-Kemp proposal for a 15 per cent tax cut as an irresponsible budget-buster.

He called this "a risky $550 billion tax scheme that would blow a hole in the (federal) deficit ... and knock our economy off-track." Gore added: "We stopped that plan before and we will stop it again."

The two running-mates met in their only televised debate less than four weeks before the Nov. 5 election. Kemp's job was to do what he could to help Dole whittle down Clinton's solid polling leads while Gore's was to hold the line for his front-running ticket.

They started all sweetness and light. Kemp waved aside an opportunity to attack Clinton's ethical standards by saying, "Bob Dole and myself do not see Al Gore and Bill Clinton as our enemy, we see them as opponents." Gore, standing a few feet away on a theatre stage, smiled and replied, "I'd like to thank Jack Kemp for the answer that he just gave."
